Area.evidence_source: They were action-oriented at transitions in life, whether these involved illness or other loss. A doctor told us about one of the elderly who had had a stroke: "He came to me after the stroke, and he'd cycled two thousand kilometers during the summer. He didn't seem like a patient who had just sat down and given up!"One daughter also described her father's behavior after his wife died: "When she passed on he had to cook, iron, wash clothes – everything. But he didn't just sit down. He got on with it straightaway!"They also confronted age by being active. They worked, and they did not give up even though age gradually made them weaker.
